findings.problem: PacketWorkflow uses pub String for status, pub bool for is_validated and is_sent, and Option<u64> for sent_at_epoch_ms. This allows illegal states such as status="sent" with is_sent=false, or is_validated=false with is_sent=true.
findings.failure_mode: Any caller can construct or mutate PacketWorkflow into a logically impossible state (e.g., packet marked sent before validation), breaking workflow invariants at runtime with no compile-time protection.
findings.fix: Replace status: String with an enum PacketStatus { Pending, Validated, Sent } and combine is_validated, is_sent, sent_at_epoch_ms into a single typestate enum or sealed struct with a fallible constructor that rejects invalid combinations.

findings.problem: is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool are independent lifecycle booleans. The valid state machine is: Pending -> Validated -> Sent, but these two bools allow all four combinations including Pending+Sent and Unvalidated+Sent.
findings.failure_mode: Workflow logic that checks is_sent without checking is_validated can process packets that were never validated. The boolean lattice has 4 states but only 3 are valid (pending, validated, sent), and the 4th is silently accepted.
findings.fix: Use a single enum PacketState { Pending, Validated, Sent } that encodes the full lifecycle. Remove is_validated and is_sent fields entirely. Derive sent_at_epoch_ms from Sent variant.

findings.problem: status: String accepts arbitrary values ("sent", "", "SENT", "deleted", etc.) with no domain-level constraints. The only valid statuses are a small finite set.
findings.failure_mode: Downstream code comparing status == "sent" is fragile (case sensitivity, typos) and the struct accepts garbage values like status="deleted" that the domain has no handling for.
findings.fix: Replace with: pub enum PacketStatus { Pending, Validated, Sent }. All status comparisons become exhaustive enum match.

findings.problem: mark_sent mutates PacketWorkflow in place, setting status="sent" and is_sent=true redundantly. The function accepts ownership but produces a mutated copy, which is both wasteful and error-prone.
findings.failure_mode: A caller could hold the original item and the returned item, observe inconsistent state. Also, mark_sent does not check that is_validated was true before allowing the sent transition, violating the state machine invariant.
findings.fix: Make mark_sent a fallible constructor: pub fn mark_sent(item: PacketWorkflow) -> Result<PacketWorkflow, PacketWorkflowError> that validates is_validated was true and returns Err for invalid transitions. Or better, make it a method on a typestate-gated handle.

findings.problem: All fields of PacketWorkflow are pub, allowing external code to mutate fields directly and bypass any invariants the module author intended.
findings.failure_mode: External crates can do item.status = "whatever" or item.is_sent = false, completely breaking internal invariants without any module-level control.
findings.fix: Make all fields private (remove pub). Provide immutable accessors (methods) for read-only access. Construction should go through fallible constructors or builder patterns.

findings.problem: No domain error enum exists (e.g., PacketError). mark_sent returns PacketWorkflow directly with no way to express why a transition failed.
findings.failure_mode: Callers cannot distinguish between 'packet was already sent', 'packet was not validated', or 'packet id was invalid'. All failures are lost or require panicking.
findings.fix: Define: pub enum PacketError { NotValidated, AlreadySent, InvalidId }. Make mark_sent return Result<PacketWorkflow, PacketError>.

findings.problem: No benchmarks, profiler data, or allocation evidence exists for this crate. No performance claims are stated, but the String-based id and status fields cause heap allocations on every struct copy.
findings.failure_mode: In hot paths, every mark_sent call allocates a new String for status via "sent".to_string() and copies the id String. For high-throughput packet processing this is a measurable allocation tax.
findings.fix: Replace id: String and status: String with &str at the parse boundary or with interned IDs (e.g., Arc str or a domain newtype). Add a benchmark measuring mark_sent throughput with baseline and second-ring evidence.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for mark_sent allocation cost (String copy + status allocation on every call)
no profiler data for hot-path packet processing throughput
no allocation evidence (no `--measure-allocations` or heaptrack/bencher data)
no behavior tests exist for state machine transitions or invalid state rejection
no command evidence for cargo test, cargo fmt, or cargo clippy
residual_risk: Static review only; no commands run. The struct has zero compile-time invariants — all state machine violations are silent at runtime. Without typestate enums and a fallible constructor, illegal states remain fully constructable. This crate in its current form violates the Holzman Rust core contract on make-illegal-states-unrepresentable, boolean lifecycle flags, and primitive-string domain modeling.
